channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average finds out the ceasefire was load-bearing
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) fell about 1.2% on Wednesday, a near 600-point slide that settled just under 50,250 after tagging session lows around 50,150.

item.title: Canadian Dollar struggles for direction as Bank of Canada keeps interest rates unchanged
item.description: The Canadian Dollar (CAD) pares some of its gains against the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday after a brief bout of strength following the Bank of Canada's (BoC) monetary policy announcement. At the time of writing, USD/CAD trades around 1.3925, recovering from an intraday low of 1.3899.

item.title: WTI Crude Oil climbs as Trump warns Iran, EIA reports deeper US stock draw
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) trades around $89.40 at the time of writing on Wednesday, up 2.33% on the day, as investors return to the Oil market following a strong rebound driven by geopolitical tensions in the Middle East.

item.title: Silver price falls toward two‑month low as rising Fed hike bets pressure XAG/USD
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) remains under pressure on Wednesday and trades around $64.70 at the time of writing, down 1.02% on the day.

item.title: British Pound hovers near 1.3400 as hot US CPI weighs on USD
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) rises by over 0.19% on Wednesday after US inflation matched estimates, though the headline Consumer Price Index (CPI) reached a three-year high in May. The GBP/USD pair trades near 1.3400 after bouncing off daily lows of 1.3362.

item.title: Australian Dollar loses ground for fourth day as NAB forecasts future RBA rate cuts
item.description: The AUD/USD pair trades near 0.7020 on Wednesday, as the Australian Dollar (AUD) continues to lose value after the latest United States (US) inflation report was released mostly in line with expectations, reinforcing the view that the Federal Reserve (Fed) could keep interest rates elevated for long

item.title: Gold falls over 3% as US inflation data sustains Fed hike expectations
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) remains under pressure on Wednesday as the latest US inflation data broadly matched market expectations and did little to alter expectations that the Federal Reserve could raise interest rates later this year.

item.title: Denmark: Core inflation rise as headline stays below Euro area – Nordea
item.description: Nordea’s Jan Størup Nielsen notes that Danish consumer prices rose 1.9% year-over-year in May, with core inflation at 2.1%, its highest level since the start of 2024. Monthly inflation was driven by higher hotel and travel prices, while food and non-alcoholic beverages fell.

item.title: BoC's Macklem: The economy is not in recession
item.description: Bank of Canada (BoC) Governor Tiff Macklem took questions from reporters, offering markets a clearer sense of how the central bank was thinking. His remarks followed the widely expected decision to keep the policy rate on hold at 2.25%.

item.title: Euro steadies as markets digest US inflation data and await ECB decision
item.description: The Euro (EUR) holds modest gains against the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday as the Greenback comes under modest pressure following the release of US inflation data. At the time of writing, EUR/USD trades around 1.15548, up 0.15% on the day.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Bearish outlook against USD as BoJ hike priced – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank’s Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret say the Japanese Yen (JPY) is soft and underperforming most G10 currencies despite stronger Producer Price Index (PPI) data, with markets fully pricing a 25 bps Bank of Japan (BoJ) hike next week and another by December.

item.title: US Dollar: Uptrend seen intact into FOMC – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists note that a softer United States (US) core Consumer Price Index (CPI) print triggered only modest US Dollar (USD) weakness. They argue the broad USD uptrend remains in place, supported by strong payrolls and geopolitical tensions.

item.title: Mexican Peso: Softer carry but relative support – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank strategists Molly Schwartz and Christian Lawrence discusses Mexico in its latest Mexican Peso (MXN) Market Musings, noting that the Mexican Peso has gained against the US Dollar (USD) year-to-date but weakened recently.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar trades sideways after mixed China data, three-year high US inflation
item.description: NZD/USD trades around 0.5815 at the time of writing on Wednesday, little changed on the day, as investors digest a series of macroeconomic releases from China and the United States (US).

item.title: Czech Koruna: Early CNB hikes support CZK outlook – ING
item.description: ING’s Frantisek Taborsky notes Czech inflation has surprised on the downside, but strong wage growth and stable core inflation keep the Czech National Bank on track for a rate hike at its June meeting.

item.title: British Pound: Holds gains against US Dollar with limited data risk – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank’s Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note GBP/USD is slightly higher, British Pound (GBP) outperforming most G10 peers except the Canadian Dollar (CAD) and Norwegian Krone (NOK), as traders await UK trade and industrial production data before the June 18 BoE meeting.

item.title: Euro: Supported by heavy sovereign issuance – BNY
item.description: BNY highlights that European governments have raised a record USD 504 billion via syndicated bonds in 2026, driven by defense, infrastructure and energy-transition spending. Despite higher yields and rate uncertainty, demand remains strong, helping governments manage refinancing needs.

item.title: Norwegian Krone: Hawkish Norges Bank underpins strength – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad reports that the Norwegian Krone is outperforming as underlying inflation overshot expectations in May, bringing forward rate hike bets from November to September.

item.title: Brent: Limited reaction to US–Iran strikes – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Hardman and Lockhart report that Brent Oil prices have shown a muted response to renewed US–Iran military exchanges, trading near recent lows after briefly dipping below USD 90 per barrel.

item.title: Canadian Dollar gains as US inflation data fails to boost the US Dollar, BoC decision eyed
item.description: The Canadian Dollar (CAD) strengthens against the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday as traders digest the latest US Consumer Price Index (CPI) data and await the Bank of Canada's (BoC) interest rate decision.

item.title: Breaking: United States CPI inflation rises to three-year high at 4.2% in May
item.description: Annual inflation in the United States (US), as measured by the change in the Consumer Price Index (CPI), rose to its highest level in three years at 4.2% in May, from 3.8% in April. This reading came in line with the market expectation.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Range-bound outlook near 0.70–0.71 against US Dollar
item.description: Rabobank’s Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley highlights that the Australian Dollar (AUD) has fallen from a top G10 performer to the bottom of recent rankings as growth momentum fades and USD strength weighs.

item.title: Aluminium: Exports and speculative longs increase – ING
item.description: ING strategists Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey highlight that Chinese unwrought Aluminium and product exports rose strongly in May to the highest level since November 2024, helped by overseas demand after Middle East disruptions.

item.title: WTI Oil price bounces back to near $88 as Trump warns further military actions against Iran
item.description: The West Texas Intermediate (WTI), futures on NYMEX, turns flat slightly above $88.00 in the European trade on Wednesday after clawing back its early losses.

item.title: South African Rand: Growth quality weighs on ZAR – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Volkmar Baur notes that stronger-than-expected South African GDP growth masks weak underlying domestic demand, with consumption and private investment soft while government spending dominates.

item.title: Japanese Yen hits fresh lows at 160.50 US Dollar as BoJ’s Ueda is hospitalized
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) extends its decline on Wednesday, threading further beyond the key 160.00 per US Dollar (USD), which is considered a red zone for Tokyo intervention.

item.title: US President Trump says he is close to ordering new strikes against Iranian infrastructure
item.description: United States (US) President Donald Trump has stated in an interview with Fox News that he is close to ordering new military strikes against Iranian power plants and bridges, adding that Tehran is "taking too long to make a deal".

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Flows reverse as BoC looms – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Bob Savage highlights a sharp reversal in Canadian Dollar (CAD) flows ahead of the June Bank of Canada (BoC) decision versus April, when CAD was generally bid.

item.title: US Dollar: Upside risks persist on sticky inflation – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes that the US Dollar retains upside risk as US inflation is expected to heat up in May and the disinflation trend has stalled.

item.title: Canada: Oil-driven inflation shifts BoC outlook – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ Robert Both updates Canada’s macro outlook as higher Oil prices push WTI above $95 through Q4, lifting headline CPI to an average 2.9% over Q2/Q3.
